title: ChatGPT Wallet: How Dots Pay, 4 Card Partners, What Stores Do
desc: ChatGPT Wallet lets a dot pay a store with a card token after you approve each buy by Face ID or fingerprint. US Pro users only, 4 card partners; no Wallet-specific integration for stores.
keywords: chatgpt wallet, openai wallet, how does chatgpt wallet work, chatgpt wallet cards, chatgpt wallet debit card, chatgpt agent payments, agentic commerce, accept chatgpt wallet payments, chatgpt dots purchases, web bot auth chatgpt
question: How does ChatGPT Wallet work, and what must an online store do so ChatGPT agents can buy from it?
cta: Want ChatGPT's agents to find and buy from your store?
body:
Short answer. ChatGPT Wallet, which OpenAI launched on November 13, 2026, lets a ChatGPT agent called a dot pay a store for you with a payment token instead of your real card number, after you approve each purchase with Face ID or a fingerprint. At launch it is limited to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 or older with eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard or Visa credit cards, the 4 card partners OpenAI names. For stores, OpenAI says Wallet works with existing checkout pages and needs no Wallet-specific integration, but bot defenses and fraud filters can still block it.

On 16 November 2026 we read OpenAI's announcement, its Help Center article Making purchases with ChatGPT Wallet, the Wallet terms and Wallet privacy notice (both effective November 12, 2026), the merchant guides in OpenAI's Commerce Partner Playbook and its Pro plans page. We checked the launch details against CNBC's report. Wallet is rolling out gradually, so some details may change.

What ChatGPT Wallet is

ChatGPT Wallet is a saved card inside ChatGPT that your dot can use to finish checkout on a store's website. OpenAI built it with American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa, according to the announcement. If you are new to dots, our guide to OpenAI dots explains what they are and what they cost. This guide covers only the payment step.

Wallet is not a bank account. The Wallet terms say it does not hold a balance, lend money or move funds, and that OpenAI is not a bank, card issuer, payment network or merchant. The store is the seller and merchant of record, so your purchase is between you and the store under its prices, shipping rules and return policy.

OpenAI describes Wallet as the first wallet that lets agents pay without seeing users' real card details while requiring a security check on every purchase. That is OpenAI's own claim. It also says users keep their card rewards and their protections for eligible disputes, such as a defective item.

Who can use it and which cards work

The rules below come from the Help Center article and the Wallet terms, with plan prices from OpenAI's Pro plans page.

RequirementWhat OpenAI says
PlanChatGPT Pro, listed at $100, $200 or $500 a month, billed monthly
LocationLive in the US, have a US billing address and use Wallet in the US
Age18 or older
CardsUS-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa credit cards
Not supportedDebit cards, and virtual cards at launch
Chase cardsPrimary cardholder only, with the connection approved in the Chase app
Business cardsAllowed if your organization permits you to store the card
Where it runsConversations with a dot, not Chat, Work or standalone Codex threads
Approval deviceA supported device with biometrics such as Face ID or Touch ID

Even eligible Pro users may not see Wallet yet, because OpenAI is turning it on gradually.

How a ChatGPT Wallet purchase works, step by step

  1. Set up a dot. Wallet only works inside a conversation with your dot.
  2. Add a card. Ask your dot to help you add a card, or open Settings, then Wallet, then Add Card. Type the card details only into the secure form, never into the chat. American Express cards use the 4-digit code on the front. Your bank may ask you to verify the card, and the terms say your issuer or OpenAI's payment provider may place a temporary verification hold that is reversed afterward.
  3. Shop. Ask your dot to find what you want. At checkout, it asks you to review and approve the purchase.
  4. Review. The approval screen shows the store, the items and quantity, the total or maximum price with known taxes, fees and shipping, the card, and whether the purchase creates a recurring charge, a deposit or a hold.
  5. Approve. Select Approve and pass a biometric check such as Face ID or Touch ID. If your current device cannot do that, a link or QR code moves the approval to a supported device on the same account.
  6. Pay by token. The payment network issues a token with its own card number, security code and expiry date. The store receives the token, the charge lands on your real card, and the number shown at checkout may differ from the one on your physical card.
  7. Confirm. The Help Center says "Ready to check out" means your approval went through, not that the store accepted the order. Look for the store's own confirmation before you try again.

Spending controls and limits

Today the main control is the approval itself. Under the Wallet terms, your approval covers only the store, items, amount, card, recipient and delivery details you were shown. If a material detail changes before the order is submitted, Wallet asks you to approve again.

The terms also allow you to give ChatGPT authority to approve purchases in advance. OpenAI's announcement says that over time it expects users to delegate purchases within limits they set, such as a spending amount, a category or a time period, with extra safeguards. It has not said when.

OpenAI keeps the right to set limits by transaction, merchant, category, card, account, device or location, and to block or delay a payment. We found no published dollar cap per purchase or per month. Your card issuer still decides whether to authorize each charge. Wallet may not be used for fraud, money laundering, cash-equivalent transactions, illegal goods or sanctions evasion.

Your card list shows each card's nickname, last four digits and expiry; you can change the default or remove one. Removing a card does not cancel an order already placed.

What ChatGPT Wallet costs users and stores

For shoppers. Wallet needs a ChatGPT Pro plan, and OpenAI's Pro plans page lists Pro at $100, $200 or $500 a month. The announcement, the Help Center article and the Wallet terms list no separate Wallet fee. The terms say your card agreement still applies, including any interest, fees, rewards and currency conversion.

For stores. OpenAI's Accept payments guide says Wallet works with existing checkout pages and payment forms, and your checkout processes the payment. The guide lists no Wallet fee. CNBC reported on launch day that OpenAI said it is not taking a cut of transactions to start; we did not find that statement on OpenAI's own pages.

Security, refunds and who to contact

The privacy notice says a service provider collects your card details, and OpenAI receives a token plus limited details such as the network, issuer and last four digits, never the full card number or security code. The store receives a network token rather than your card number. If the biometric check runs on your device, the terms say OpenAI does not receive your face or fingerprint scan. OpenAI says it does not sell Wallet data or share it for targeted advertising, but it may share device and fraud signals with stores so they can judge whether an order is genuine.

Refunds work the way they do when you shop yourself. The Help Center splits support like this:

ProblemWho handles it
Order status, cancellation, return or refundThe store, under its own policy
Recurring charge you want to stopThe store
Declined, pending, disputed or unrecognized chargeYour card issuer
Wallet error, account break-in, or a purchase that differs from what you approvedOpenAI Support

The terms say OpenAI does not decide or fund refunds or chargebacks unless the law requires it or OpenAI promises otherwise. If you approve a subscription, the store may keep the payment credential and charge it again under the plan you agreed to.

Which stores ChatGPT Wallet works with

OpenAI publishes no list of stores. The Help Center says Wallet may not be able to complete checkout at every store. On the merchant side, OpenAI's agent access page says ChatGPT's cloud browser can already use a site without being added to an allowlist, and the payments guide says Wallet works with existing checkouts. What can stop it is the store's own defenses: bot rules and fraud systems that read the cloud browser as a bot.

Some large sellers are opting out. CNBC reported that Amazon prevents agents from buying on its platform and that United Airlines said it will block agents from booking tickets.

What a store should do so ChatGPT agents can buy

OpenAI's Partner Playbook lists six areas. These are the ones that matter most for an online store.

  • Get found. Claim your business in Business Hub, verify your identity, then upload a product feed by manual upload, a hosted HTTPS URL or SFTP, with full snapshots and stable item_id values, per the feed guide. Shopify merchants can connect from Business Hub or the Shopify admin, and OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT post says eligible Shopify products already reach ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog. A feed puts your catalog in front of the agent; being the store ChatGPT names when someone asks for a recommendation depends on your pages, and ChatGPT also draws on the public web, per OpenAI's playbook, which is the work of our AI search optimization service.
  • Let the cloud browser in. The agent access page says 4 providers verify ChatGPT's signed requests automatically: Akamai, Cloudflare, HUMAN and Vercel. On Cloudflare, go to Security, then Settings, then AI Crawler and Agent access policies, and set "dots, OpenAI" under Personal Agents to Allow, or write a WAF rule that allows Bot Detection ID 129220581. Other firewalls need manual Web Bot Auth checks. These visits are separate from OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, so allowing one does not change how you treat the other.
  • Tune your fraud rules. OpenAI is starting to pass shopper signals in the Forwarded HTTP header, with up to 7 parameters: asn, for, ip-country, ip-prefix, locale, tz and user-agent. Ask your fraud and payment providers whether they read it. The announcement names 7 partners: Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd for fraud prevention, and Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe as payment providers.
  • Handle the token correctly. You receive a network token, not the card number; the payments guide says to use the Payment Account Reference (PAR) to link it to the underlying account. Do not reuse the token for a separate purchase. For subscriptions, get the customer's consent and follow your processor's rules for merchant-initiated charges.
  • Treat agent orders as customer orders. OpenAI's agent access page says support for payment or order errors should work as if the customer had acted personally.
  • Go further if it pays. A plugin lets agents check stock or manage carts through your own systems, and websites can add WebMCP tools. Neither is required for Wallet.

Limits and risks to weigh

  • Small audience for now. Per OpenAI's announcement, Wallet starts with Pro subscribers only, in the US only, aged 18 or older, with credit cards only, and a gradual rollout.
  • No merchant controls yet. OpenAI's agent access page says site owners cannot yet limit which actions users take through the agent. It says it requires human review before any consequential action.
  • Agents make mistakes. The Wallet terms warn that AI systems can make mistakes and tell users to approve only correct orders. Plan for returns on agent orders as you would for any order.
  • Failed checkouts can lead to retries. OpenAI's Help Center tells shoppers to look for the store's confirmation before retrying a failed checkout, so a clear confirmation page and email help avoid duplicates.
  • OpenAI is not the seller. The terms say the store is merchant of record, and OpenAI does not decide or fund refunds or chargebacks unless the law requires it.

How imisofts can help

imisofts is a Dubai agency that builds AI automation and Shopify and e-commerce systems. For Wallet readiness, we can review your CDN and firewall rules against OpenAI's agent access guide, prepare a product feed for Business Hub, and connect order and support flows so agent-placed orders are handled like any other. See our AI automation for e-commerce page for how we scope that work.

What to do this week

  • If you shop with a dot: look for Wallet in Settings, add a credit card rather than a debit card, read the full approval screen including recurring terms, and keep the store's confirmation for every order.
  • If you run a store: ask whoever manages your CDN or firewall to check the ChatGPT agent rule (on Cloudflare, "dots, OpenAI" set to Allow).
  • Ask your fraud tool and payment provider whether they read the Forwarded header and how they treat agent purchases.
  • Claim your business in Business Hub, or connect your Shopify store from the Shopify admin, and plan a product feed.
  • Tell your support team that orders placed by an agent are the customer's own orders.
faqs: ChatGPT Wallet is an OpenAI feature, launched on November 13, 2026, that lets a ChatGPT agent called a dot pay a store on your behalf. You save a card once, approve each purchase with a biometric check such as Face ID or Touch ID, and the payment network gives the store a payment token instead of your real card number. The store remains the seller and merchant of record.
Who can use ChatGPT Wallet, and which cards work?

At launch, US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 or older with a US billing address. Eligible cards are US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa credit cards. Debit cards are not supported, virtual cards are not supported at launch, and Chase cards must belong to the primary cardholder. OpenAI is rolling Wallet out gradually, so some eligible users may not see it yet.

Wallet needs a ChatGPT Pro plan, which OpenAI lists at $100, $200 or $500 a month. OpenAI's announcement, Help Center article and Wallet terms list no separate Wallet fee. Your card agreement still applies, including any interest, fees and currency conversion.
Does the store or OpenAI see my card number?

No. According to OpenAI's Wallet privacy notice, a service provider collects your card details and OpenAI receives only a token and limited details such as the last four digits, not the full number or security code. The store receives a network token with its own card number, security code and expiry date.
How do I get a refund for a ChatGPT Wallet purchase?

Contact the store, which handles cancellations, returns and refunds under its own policy. For a declined, disputed or unrecognized charge, contact your card issuer. Contact OpenAI Support for Wallet errors or a purchase that differs from what you approved. OpenAI's terms say it does not decide or fund refunds or chargebacks unless the law requires it.
How does an online store accept ChatGPT Wallet payments?

OpenAI says Wallet works with existing checkout pages and payment forms, with no Wallet-specific integration. The practical steps are to make sure your CDN or firewall does not block ChatGPT's verified cloud browser, ask your fraud and payment providers whether they read the Forwarded header OpenAI sends, and use the Payment Account Reference to link the network token to the underlying account.
